title: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

reading.body:
The failure is a synthetic edit to a documentary photograph of identifiable people, published as though it were the original. The picture was taken at a Lunar New Year party and posted by the university dining service, then reused on campus banners with one student replaced by a different person and the other students altered in appearance. The edit occurred in the production of advertising material, and the banner carried no disclosure that the image had been changed.

Catching it would have taken a comparison against the source photograph before the banners were displayed. Stanford's AI policy prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities or achievements, and the university has said the alteration and the lack of disclosure violated that policy. The change was noticed instead by a friend of the student who had been removed, after the image was already in public use. The university has said it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises on additional training and proper review of all materials.

What is not established is who performed the edit, whether anyone approved it, or whether the substitution was intended. The university's acknowledgement covers the fact of the alteration and the policy breach, not intent.

reports.title: Stanford Used A.I. to Swap Black Student for Hispanic Student in a Photo
Stanford R&DE Uses AI to Race Swap Students for Advertising
University confirms use of AI-edited photo amid controversy
Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad

summary:
In 2024, a Stanford photographer took a picture of Billy Ramirez, a Hispanic senior majoring in human biology, with two other students at a Lunar New Year party. The university dining service posted the photo online the next day. Last week, when Stanford used the image on campus banners, Ramirez had been replaced by a Black woman, and the other students appeared thinner. Ramirez learned about it from a friend and said he was upset and frustrated, though he also saw a comedic element.

Stanford acknowledged on Tuesday that it had used artificial intelligence to change the original image. The university said its AI policy strictly prohibits using AI to produce or alter images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements. It said the alteration and lack of disclosure violated that policy. Stanford added that it is working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials.
title_en: Stanford violated its AI policy by turning a Hispanic student into a fake Black woman in ad
